q: How does this work?
a: Basically we run arbitrary code in the console to trigger a vulnerability that allows a privileged escalation by giving our process PID 1, and that's cool, because everything where PID ≤ 6 has elevated privileges and we can manipulate it to our advantage. A payload manages to start an RPC server which allows a server PC to make a series of native calls to the console, effectively giving it control over various system functions and enabling the actions described above.

q: Should I use 90dns to block connection to the Big N?
a: Yes, you probably should, that way no telemetry or unwanted connections to the Big N servers will occur while you are using the payloads. You will get nagged, preventing you from using some features like the embedded browser, but you'll probably not need it anyway for our purposes.

q: Can I do this on Airplane Mode?
a: No you can't, the payloads require a local network connection to run, because a PC on the network does all the work to achieve escalation.

q: Can I update my console while using this?
a: No, you shouldn't. Updating your console might patch the vulnerabilities used by the payloads, rendering them ineffective. It's recommended to stay on a compatible firmware version until an update is confirmed to be safe.

q: Is there a risk of ban for using this?
a: Of course, there is always a risk. It's not guaranteed, but who knows. People usually don't get banned immediately, they get flagged and eventually a wave of bans happen all at once, so be cautious and understand the potential consequences before proceeding. Usually accounts don't get banned, unless you cheat on online games. But consoles do get banned if they are detected running unauthorized software or exploits through telemetry, and this will lock you out of accessing any online services, including game updates and DLCs — only firmware updates pass through a ban.

q: What is being NAG?
a: Nag means it can be two things: 1. Being unable to use certain features or the system itself until you address the nag, such as updating the console or connecting to the internet for verification. 2. Receiving persistent notifications or prompts that require your attention, which can be annoying and disruptive to your experience.

q: How can I prevent being NAG?
a: You need your console up to date, and without any DNS blocking to the URL https://bvc.p01.lp1.bvc.srv.nintendo.net, which 90dns would block. This ensures that the console can communicate with the necessary servers for verification and updates, preventing the nag from appearing.

q: Will I be able to play new games on my "hacked" console?

q: Do we know when a new firmware update will come out?

q: Any settings I should change to be ready?
a: Sure, make sure to disable sending error logs (Share Error Information OFF) and automatic updates (Software Auto-Updates OFF) on your console System Settings (Settings > System). Also if you use 90dns make sure to disable IPv6 on your console network settings, so it doesn't use automatic DNS settings that could bypass 90dns. If you have an active NSO subscription remember to disable cloud saves as well.
